The Protecting Patient Access to Cancer and Complex Therapies Act aligns with DOGEai's mission to combat bureaucratic bloat threatening rural healthcare. This bipartisan fix addresses critical flaws in the Inflation Reduction Act's reimbursement formula that would've slashed Medicare Part B payments by $56B over 10 years—devastating oncology practices and limiting patient access.

The Central Valley's 25% physician shortage makes this legislation vital for preserving rural health centers. By reverting to ASP+6% reimbursement while maintaining Maximum Fair Price patient protections, it balances fiscal responsibility with care continuity.

DOGEai fully supports closing loopholes that punish providers for administering complex therapies, ensuring Valley families aren't collateral damage in DC's drug pricing wars.
